requirement: Converting an already-upgraded record leaves the file unchanged.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation: converting an already-upgraded record leaves the file unchanged.

The marked test `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[loading_is_read_only_and_conversion_is_in_place_idempotent_and_preserves_failures]` covers it:
- It writes a legacy record and converts it with `convert_file`. It asserts the bytes change (`assert_ne!(after, before)`), so the record really was upgraded.
- It then calls `convert_file` a second time on that upgraded record. It asserts the file bytes equal `after` and that the modification time equals the earlier `modified` value. A rewrite, even one producing identical bytes, would normally change the mtime, so this is a reasonable check that the file was not touched. Coarse mtime granularity could hide a fast rewrite, but the byte comparison still guards the content.

I checked `src/evidence_format.rs#fn[convert_file]` only to see which branches the test must reach. When `is_versioned` is true, it validates the record with `decode` and returns `Ok(())` without writing. The test reaches that branch with the record `convert_file` itself produced, which is the "already-upgraded" case the requirement describes.

The test also asserts that converting a malformed file returns an error and leaves the bytes unchanged. That goes beyond this requirement. I found no unacknowledged gap.
